recommendations.title: Eliminate render-blocking resources
recommendations.description: Resources are blocking the first paint of your page. Consider delivering critical JS/CSS inline and deferring all non-critical JS/styles. Learn how to eliminate render-blocking resources.

recommendations.title: Properly size images

recommendations.title: Reduce unused CSS
recommendations.description: Reduce unused rules from stylesheets and defer CSS not used for above-the-fold content to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. Learn how to reduce unused CSS.

recommendations.title: Reduce unused JavaScript
recommendations.description: Reduce unused JavaScript and defer loading scripts until they are required to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. Learn how to reduce unused JavaScript.

recommendations.title: Serve images in next-gen formats
recommendations.description: Image formats like WebP and AVIF often provide better compression than PNG or JPEG, which means faster downloads and less data consumption. Learn more about modern image formats.

recommendations.title: Reduce JavaScript execution time
recommendations.description: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling, and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this. Learn how to reduce Javascript execution time.

recommendations.description: Consider reducing the time spent parsing, compiling and executing JS. You may find delivering smaller JS payloads helps with this. Learn how to minimize main-thread work

recommendations.description: Third-party code can significantly impact load performance. Limit the number of redundant third-party providers and try to load third-party code after your page has primarily finished loading. Learn how to minimize third-party impact.

aiSummaries.text:
**Executive Summary**  
The website crawl analysis of **https://contentbloom.com** reveals a critically low page count of only 2 pages, which significantly limits the site's discoverability, user engagement, and SEO potential. This finding indicates a high-priority issue that requires immediate attention to ensure the site can effectively serve its business purpose.

**Key Findings**  
- **Finding**: Only 2 pages were crawled.  
  **Business Impact**: Severely limits search engine visibility, reduces user engagement, and undermines the site's ability to drive conversions or deliver content effectively.  
  **Priority**: High  
  **Recommended Action**: Investigate and resolve the root cause (e.g., robots.txt restrictions, noindex tags, or technical crawl barriers) to ensure all intended pages are accessible to search engines and users.  

**Recommended Next Step**  
Conduct a comprehensive technical audit to identify and resolve any crawl barriers, ensuring all critical pages are indexed and accessible.

aiSummaries.text:
### Executive Summary  
All 2 scanned pages of the ContentBloom website contain broken links, including critical links on the homepage and a blog post. This poses an immediate risk to user experience, SEO, and brand credibility.  

### Key Findings  
1. **Finding**: Broken Facebook link (`https://www.facebook.com/contentbloomwcm/`) on the homepage and blog post (400 error).  
   - **Business Impact**: Disrupts customer journeys, reduces social engagement, and harms SEO due to poor user experience.  
   - **Priority**: High  
   - **Recommended Action**: Immediately update the Facebook link to the correct URL or remove it if no longer relevant.  

2. **Finding**: Broken internal link (`https://contentbloom.com/xmlrpc.php`) on the homepage and blog post (405 error).  
   - **Business Impact**: Hinders site navigation, potentially affecting conversions and user trust.  
   - **Priority**: Medium  
   - **Recommended Action**: Investigate and fix the internal link or redirect it to a relevant page.  

3. **Finding**: 100% of scanned pages contain broken links.  
   - **Business Impact**: Indicates systemic issues with link maintenance, risking broader SEO penalties and user frustration.  
   - **Priority**: High  
   - **Recommended Action**: Conduct a full site audit to identify and fix all broken links.  

### Recommended Next Step  
Perform a comprehensive broken link audit across the entire website and prioritize fixing the Facebook link and internal link identified in this scan.

aiSummaries.text:
### Executive Summary  
The website’s mobile performance is critically poor, with an average score of 34, significantly lagging behind desktop performance (74). This disparity risks alienating mobile users, who represent a substantial portion of web traffic, potentially impacting user experience, engagement, and conversions.

### Key Findings  
1. **Finding:** Mobile performance is severely lacking, with one page scoring as low as 21.  
   **Business Impact:** Poor mobile performance can lead to higher bounce rates, reduced user engagement, and lower conversion rates, especially on critical pages like the blog post.  
   **Priority:** High  
   **Recommended Action:** Prioritize optimizing mobile performance by addressing render-blocking resources, properly sizing images, and minifying CSS, as these changes can yield significant improvements.  

2. **Finding:** Render-blocking resources are prevalent across 4 pages, with estimated savings of up to 1,370 ms on mobile.  
   **Business Impact:** Render-blocking resources delay page load times, frustrating users and negatively impacting SEO rankings.  
   **Priority:** High  
   **Recommended Action:** Eliminate render-blocking resources to improve load times and enhance user experience, particularly on mobile.  

3. **Finding:** Unused and unminified CSS affects 3 pages, with potential savings of 10–111 KiB.  
   **Business Impact:** Excessive CSS increases page size and load times, slowing down user interactions and reducing overall site efficiency.  
   **Priority:** Medium  
   **Recommended Action:** Minify and reduce unused CSS to streamline page performance and improve load times.  

### Recommended Next Step  
Immediately address mobile performance issues by eliminating render-blocking resources and optimizing CSS, focusing on the worst-performing pages to maximize impact.
